crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: FAIR Data
children.blurb: FAIR Data is a set of principles for making research data Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable.

children.name: Metadata and Ontologies
children.blurb: Metadata and ontologies in research data and repositories cover the structured descriptions that make data, papers, models, and tools discoverable and the formal vocabularies that give those descriptions shared meaning.

children.name: Federated Sharing of Sensitive Data
children.blurb: Federated sharing of sensitive data covers arrangements where separate organizations or repositories keep data in place and exchange only models, statistics, or encrypted intermediate results.

children.name: Institutional Knowledge Graphs
children.blurb: Institutional knowledge graphs are structured representations of an organization's people, projects, publications, datasets, instruments, and administrative units, with typed relationships between them.

children.name: Long-Term Digital Preservation
children.blurb: Long-term digital preservation is the set of policies, technologies and practices that keep research data and repository objects readable, usable and authentic for decades or longer.

sections.body: Research data and repositories is the part of AI work that treats datasets, metadata, and storage systems as first class research outputs. AI is used to extract structured claims from papers, align ontologies, detect duplicates, recommend datasets, and monitor provenance. In practice, machine learning helps tag and classify data, link terms across vocabularies, and surface relationships in large collections. Repositories use these methods to make data findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable, which is what FAIR Data describes. The work is less about building a single model and more about building durable infrastructure that many models and people depend on. This site's library, with 135 research papers and 12646 claims extracted from research works, is an example of a small but structured research collection that depends on such infrastructure.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are solved well enough for routine use. Persistent identifiers, basic metadata schemas, and repository software are mature, and many institutions can publish datasets with stable links. Ontologies and controlled vocabularies are widely used, though mapping between them remains labor intensive and often needs human review. Federated sharing of sensitive data is harder because access rules, consent, and legal constraints vary by jurisdiction and by dataset. Long term preservation is not just storage, it requires format migration, documentation, and governance across decades. AI can assist with metadata generation and anomaly detection, but it does not remove the need for curators, and automated labels can be wrong or biased.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: FAIR Data sets out the expectations for findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable research objects, and it is the natural starting point for readers who want the vocabulary. Metadata and Ontologies goes deeper into the schemas and vocabularies that make data machine readable and comparable. Federated Sharing of Sensitive Data addresses what happens when data cannot be pooled in one place, covering access control and privacy preserving analysis. Institutional Knowledge Graphs shows how an organization can connect its own papers, datasets, people, and projects into a queryable network. Long-Term Digital Preservation closes the loop by asking how all of this survives changes in software, hardware, and institutional priorities. A reader can move from FAIR Data to Metadata and Ontologies for foundations, then to Federated Sharing of Sensitive Data or Institutional Knowledge Graphs for specific architectures, and finally to Long-Term Digital Preservation for the time horizon.
